text:
alex: Heads-up — after last night's deploy I'm seeing an SSE streaming tail-latency spike on prod for tool-call responses. 95p for small payload streams jumped from ~120ms -> ~420ms.

maya: ugh. is this only for tool-call streams or regular chat streaming too?

alex: mostly tool-call paths. regular chat streams look fine. affects most models but much worse when payloads include small JSON tool outputs.

chao: did we change any serialization or chunk framing in the recent protobuf->json switch? I remember a PR touching sse framing and encoder.

alex: yes, PR 5621 changed the streaming encoder to flush per "frame" and switched to naive json.dumps for tool outputs to avoid a deepcopy. suspect it increased syscall count / write size pattern.

infra-bot: CI perf test failed: streaming-latency-check on release/2026-03-16 — regressions detected (p95 +260ms). Job: ci/streaming/perf-2026-03-16.

julian: can someone run a microprofile with strace / tcpdump on canary to see write sizes and Nagle interactions? small writes could be coalesced unpredictably.

chao: running on canary now. quick `tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/sse.pcap port 443` + `strace -e write -p $pid` to capture write syscalls. will post results in a minute.

chao: result: lots of 200-300 byte writes from the encoder when streaming tool-call tokens, plus a lot of JSON encode time in CPU profile. kernel's send path shows many syscalls per message.

alex: that matches hypothesis — more syscall overhead -> higher p95. might be exacerbated by batching heuristics: we changed to more aggressive immediate-flush for frames, so we trade latency for throughput but hitting syscall cost.

maya: two actionable routes: 1) revert PR 5621 to restore previous flush behavior, 2) keep encoder but change to coalesce small writes into a single buffer + single write call. which is faster to ship?

julian: revert is fastest for rollback. coalescing needs code change and tests but could be done in a patch. We should also check the tool-call JSON encoding path — `json.dumps` was slower than our previous ujson path for small dicts in microbench.

chao: quick microbench: for 1k small dict encodes, ujson median 0.2ms, json.dumps 0.6ms on our image. and adding a few hundred syscalls amplifies p95.

alex: can we do an emergency revert to unblock rollouts and then follow up with coalesce + switch back to ujson?

maya: +1. I'll open a revert PR and mark it rollout-blocker. also tagging platform-oncall.

infra-bot: Deploy rollback requested by maya. Rollout status: in progress.

julian: also add a perf CI test that simulates many small tool-call frames + SSE to catch this in future. add a metric for syscall counts per stream too.

chao: logging additional traces for encoder write size distribution in canary so we can validate the fix without full revert if needed.

alex: filed issue RW-987: "SSE tool-call small-write syscall overhead -> p95 regression" with suggested fixes (revert, coalesce buff, re-evaluate encoder impl).

maya: thanks. once revert lands we'll monitor p95. if revert doesn't fix, escalate. :thumbsup:

chao: test note — KV-cache miss rate increased slightly on canary during spikes, probably because more timeouts from client side caused reconnects; track but likely secondary effect.

julian: plan: revert now, follow-up patch to coalesce + restore faster JSON encoder, add CI guard. assigning owners.

alex: cool. I'll watch metrics and post updates here. Thanks folks.
